chunks: In this chain of narration, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Suraqa, from his father, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said:

Whoever recites Surah Al-Hajj every three days, his age will not end until he goes to the Sacred House of Allah, and if he dies during his journey, he will enter paradise. I asked, 'What if he is unable to do so?' He replied, 'Some of the difficulty will be alleviated for him.'

key_terms.بَيْتِ اللَّهِ الْحَرَامِ: The Sacred House of Allah (the Kaaba in Mecca)
key_terms.سُورَةَ الْحَجِّ: Surah Al-Hajj (The Pilgrimage), the 22nd chapter of the Quran
key_terms.مُخَالِفًا: One who is unable or deficient (in performing Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for reciting Surah Al-Hajj regularly according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this virtue in *Thawab al-Amal*, emphasizing the intercessory power of Surah Al-Hajj in securing the Hajj pilgrimage or its spiritual equivalent in Paradise. The hadith notably addresses the case of the 'mukhalf' (one who is not fully compliant or is in a state of sin), promising that even for them, the recitation mitigates their specific burdens, reflecting the Shia emphasis on divine mercy for the imperfect believer. This practice underscores the belief that consistent recitation serves as a spiritual preparation for the ultimate journey to the Kaaba.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1 - In this chain of narration, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Suraqa, from his father, from Abu Abdullah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (as)), he said:

"Whoever recites Surah Al-Hajj every three days, his age will not end until he goes to the Sacred House of Allah (Kaaba), and if he dies during his journey, he will enter paradise." I asked, "What if he is unable to do so?" He replied, "Some of the difficulty will be alleviated for him."
